newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-Italian PM says he is condemned to die in exile.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Italian PM says he is condemned to die in exile.

text.p: Former prime minister Bettino Craxi said on Wednesday he was condemned to die in exile following a ruling by Italy's high court to uphold prison sentences against him and nine others.

Italy's highest court on Tuesday confirmed a 5-1/2-year jail sentence for Craxi for illegal party financing and upheld convictions on corruption charges of nine other people, including Italian financier Sergio Cusani.
"I have been condemned to die in exile," Craxi, 64, said in an interview with state RAI television from his exile home in the Tunisian resort of Hammamet.
"I apologise if people think the country was damaged by the party financing," Craxi said.
"But for the rest, for what I have done, I am waiting for people to thank me," added the former Sociliast, who has said he would not return to Italy just to go to jail.

Milan magistrates have asked the Justice Ministry to issue an international arrest warrant for Craxi on the basis of the latest court decision, judicial sources said. It would be the second arrest warrant issued against him.
Craxi, premier from 1983 to 1987, faces 5-1/2 years in jail for the SAI saga and has more than 25 years of jail sentences accumulated against him from other trials.
Cusani, who helped expose rampant graft in Italy's political old guard, turned himself in to prison authorities on Wednesday to begin a four-year sentence for bribery.
He is the first major figure to go to jail after being convicted in Italy's "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) scandals.

"I am at peace with myself. I will try to build something useful for people inside prison, where life carries on even if it's not a very good life," Cusani told reporters before entering Milan's imposing San Vittore jail.

Cusani was convicted two years ago for his part in a scandal over bribes paid by insurance firm SAI to win contracts from energy group ENI. He was the main figure in another major graft trial centred on ENI which is currently under appeal.

The high court also confirmed sentences against former SAI president Salvatore Ligresti and managing director Fausto Rapisardo, former Christian Democrat party treasurer Severino Citaristi and two former ENI executives.
It also upheld a four-year conviction of Marcello Di Giovanni, the former head of insurer Padana Assicurazioni, who was arrested in Rome on Wednesday, police said.
They said they were still looking for former ENI executives Antonio Sernia and Alberto Grotti, whose arrest was requested earlier on Wednesday by the Milan prosecutor's office.

The Tangentopoli scandals, which eventually toppled Italy's political old guard, broke in February 1992 when the manager of a Milan old people's home confessed to taking bribes on behalf of Craxi's Socialist party.
